transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you saw a problem that wasn't yours to fix, and you fixed it anyway.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: Our checkout service was timing out on mobile. I traced it with Jaeger, found an N+1 query, wrote a PR with fix and benchmark showing 60% reduction, got it merged in three hours, and added a monitor.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate on a technical decision.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: My counterpart wanted to deploy a ranking model to 100% traffic. I prepared a brief with three scenarios, proposed 5% with rollback triggers, and we co-developed criteria. We caught a regression at 15%.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you were wrong about something technical.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: I advocated for a service mesh. Operational overhead was 3x my estimate. I ran a retrospective, identified I'd anchored on blog posts, and we adopted mTLS-via-gateway. I now interview two practitioners before advocating.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: What's a weakness you've had to actively work on?

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: I move to solution mode too quickly. I started structured restatement. My 360 showed improvement by four colleagues. I still have to consciously activate the habit.
